title: SharpLipschitzConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally L-Lipschitz convex function on Euclidean space. The minimum is attained.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each query at x returns the exact value f(x) together with a subgradient in one call.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The vector reply is an exact subgradient from a fixed selection g. At every x it satisfies f(y) ≥ f(x) + ⟨g(x), y − x⟩ for all y. The reply is independent of history and seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: sharpness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Global weak sharp minima with public modulus 0 < μ ≤ L. For every x there is a minimizer z with μ‖x − z‖ ≤ f(x) − f(z). The minimizing set may contain multiple points.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain and output space are ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm, and d is public.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The public starting point x₀ is within a known radius D > 0 of some minimizer. L and ε > 0 are also public. The objective, its minimum value, and a minimizing point are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SharpLipschitzConvex.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid and spec.admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point X in ℝᵈ. Its error is f(X) − f(x⋆) for a global minimizer x⋆.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output gap must be integrable and satisfy E[f(X) − f(x⋆)] ≤ ε under the execution law.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the established weak sharp minima formulation for Lipschitz convex optimization with an exact value-and-subgradient oracle and a known initial distance bound.

descriptionHtml:
Sharp Lipschitz Convex Minimization

We minimize a convex, L-Lipschitz function f:Rd→R in Euclidean dimension d≥0. Its objective gap is at least μ times the distance to the minimizer set, where 0<μ≤L. A given starting point x0 lies within distance D>0 of a minimizer x⋆. At each point x, the oracle returns f(x) and a fixed choice of subgradient. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rd with integrable gap and E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). Write X⋆=argminx∈Rdf(x) for the minimizer set and ∥⋅∥ for the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives the nonnegative integer d, the constants L,μ,D,ε, and x0∈Rd.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and Lipschitz continuity). For every x,y∈Rd and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),|f(x)−f(y)|≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and sharpness). There exists x⋆∈X⋆ with ∥x0−x⋆∥≤D. For each x∈Rd, there exists z∈X⋆ such that f(x)−f(z)≥μ∥x−z∥.

At any query point x∈Rd, the oracle returns (f(x),g(x)), where g:Rd→Rd is a fixed selection satisfying the subgradient inequality f(y)≥f(x)+⟨g(x),y−x⟩,x,y∈Rd. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must have an integrable objective gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

budget.value: fun p => ⌈4 * p.L ^ 2 / p.μ ^ 2⌉₊ * (Nat.clog 2 ⌈p.μ * p.D / p.ε⌉₊ + 1)

budgets.value: fun p => ⌈4 * p.L ^ 2 / p.μ ^ 2⌉₊ * (Nat.clog 2 ⌈p.μ * p.D / p.ε⌉₊ + 1)

theorems.referencesHtml:
• B. T. Polyak. Minimization of Unsmooth Functionals. 1969. Complexity: O((L/μ)2[1+max{0,log⁡(μD/ε)}]) value-and-subgradient calls for the best queried objective gap to reach ε, using Polyak steps with known minimum value.
  • Tianbao Yang and Qihang Lin. RSG: Beating Subgradient Method without Smoothness and Strong Convexity. 2018. Complexity: O((L/μ)2[1+max{0,log⁡(Δ/ε)}]) subgradient calls for restarted subgradient descent from a certified gap bound Δ. From radius D, one initial averaged subgradient stage costs O((L/μ)2) calls and certifies Δ=μD.
  • S. S. Ablaev, F. S. Stonyakin, M. S. Alkousa, and A. V. Gasnikov. Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Mathematical Programming Problems with Quasi-Convex Functions. 2023. Complexity: O((L/μ)2[1+max{0,log⁡(μD/ε)}]) value-and-subgradient calls for the restarted normalized subgradient method to return a point with objective gap at most ε in the unconstrained specialization.

comparisonHtml:
Convex, L-Lipschitz f:Rd→R with dist(x0,X∗)≤D and global weak sharpness f(x)−f∗≥μdist(x,X∗), where 0<μ≤L and D>0. Each oracle reply gives the exact value and a subgradient. The target is E[f(x^)−f∗]≤ε for ε>0. The displayed upper bounds give this gap guarantee deterministically.

Oracle budgets for sharp Lipschitz convex minimization.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SharpLipschitzConvexRestartedSubgradient (Ours) (review) Sufficient budget O(κ2(1+log+⁡(μD/ε))) joint calls
(2) RSG (Yang and Lin 2018), Cor. 7 (θ=1) Sufficient budget O(κ2(1+log⁡(LD/ε))) subgradient calls for ε<LD, with ε0=LD (0 if ε≥LD). (1): Distance-based tuning replaces LD by μD in the log, saving up to O(κ2log⁡κ) for μ2D/L<ε<LD. At ε=μD and κ>1, O(κ2) versus O(κ2(1+log⁡κ)). Same order for ε≤μ2D/L. With D=ε0/μ, (1) formalizes the known rate. (1): Needs global sharpness. (2) needs it only where f−f∗≤ε/2.
(3) GeomGD (Wang 2025), Thm. 1 (h(t)=μt, μ≤L/2) Sufficient budget O(κ2(1+log⁡(LD/ε))) subgradient calls for ε<LD via Lipschitz continuity (0 if ε≥LD). (1): For μ≤L/2 and μ2D/L<ε<LD, the objective-gap budget replaces LD by μD in the log. Same order for ε≤μ2D/L. (1): Needs global sharpness. (3) needs it only within distance D of X∗ and gives last-iterate accuracy.
(4) Derived bound from (3) with one final averaged subgradient phase (μ≤L/2) Sufficient budget O(κ2(1+log+⁡(μD/ε))) subgradient calls, including the final phase. (1): Matches the known rate on μ≤L/2. (1): Needs global sharpness. (4) needs it only within distance D of X∗.

Abbr: X∗=arg⁡minf, f∗=minf, κ=L/μ, log+⁡(t)=max{0,log⁡t}, and ε0 is a known upper bound on f(x0)−f∗.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.SharpLipschitzConvex

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  D : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

def IsSubgradientOracle {d : ℕ} (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ)
    (O : Oracle (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
    (∀ x y, f x + ⟪g x, y - x⟫ ≤ f y) ∧ ∀ h x s, O.answer h (0, x) s = (f x, g x)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d) → ℝ
  Query p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Reply p := ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Output p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x y, |f x - f y| ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.D) ∧
    (∀ x, ∃ z, IsMinOn f Set.univ z ∧ p.μ * ‖x - z‖ ≤ f x - f z) ∧
    IsSubgradientOracle f O
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SharpLipschitzConvex
